answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities by requiring each agent to stake a refundable deposit that is slashed if it misbehaves, with reputation earned slowly over a long horizon of verified work. A new identity starts on a small knoll of trust, able to do only low-value tasks, and must build a bridge of successful, independently attested transactions before handling larger payments. Creating thousands of fakes then costs thousands of deposits and months of honest work, while one real agent keeps its stake and history intact.
